questions.stem: What is the purpose of limestone in the blast furnace?

options.text: It acts as the reducing agent for iron ore
It provides extra carbon for the reaction
It removes impurities such as sand (silicon dioxide) as slag
It lowers the melting point of the iron

questions.explanation: Limestone (CaCO₃) decomposes to form calcium oxide (CaO), which reacts with sand (SiO₂) impurities to form calcium silicate (CaSiO₃), known as slag. The slag floats on the molten iron and can be tapped off separately.

questions.stem: Why can carbon not be used to extract aluminium from aluminium oxide?

options.text: Aluminium oxide is insoluble in water
Aluminium is above carbon in the reactivity series, so carbon cannot remove the oxygen
Carbon would react with the aluminium to form aluminium carbonate
Aluminium oxide does not contain oxygen

questions.explanation: Aluminium is above carbon in the reactivity series, meaning aluminium is more reactive than carbon. Carbon cannot remove oxygen from aluminium oxide because aluminium holds onto oxygen more strongly than carbon does. Electrolysis must be used instead.
